findings.title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty/null and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. handleNewBooking can set `destinationCalendar: null` and other handlers set `[]`. This is exactly the case the fallback is meant for: Google Meet selected with no Google calendar. It now throws instead of falling back to Cal Video, so the booking creation fails. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references lose their credentialId
findings.body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept `result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. The ternary branches were effectively swapped for non-calendar results. Video BookingReferences are now saved without a credentialId. handleCancelBooking only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling no longer deletes the video meeting for new bookings. Should be `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. `result.credentialId`).

findings.title: Fallback lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs the `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then looks for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value, which never matches. The fallback therefore always returns `undefined`; the old code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In updateEvent, `calendarId` becomes undefined for any reference without an externalCalendarId (legacy bookings), and the Google API call fails. The same pattern in deleteEvent (line ~315) silently drops the configured destination calendar and falls back to `primary`. Fall back to the main host's destination calendar's externalId instead.

findings.title: createEvent only matches destination calendar by credentialId; legacy destinations go to "primary"
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now found only via `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. EventManager still has a branch for destination calendars with no `credentialId`, where it calls `createEvent(c, event)` for every credential of that integration. For those, no destination matches, so the event is inserted into `primary` instead of the configured `destinationCalendar.externalId` as before. This is a behaviour regression for existing users whose DestinationCalendar rows lack a credentialId. Fall back to the matching-integration destination's externalId when no credentialId match exists.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId
findings.body: Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`, so the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` had a valid calendarId. Now `selectedCalendar` can be `undefined` (insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but the patch still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination matches the credential, the event is inserted into primary, but the patch that adds the Meet link to the description fails or targets nothing. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value for the patch.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services use the main host's destination for every credential
findings.body: EventManager now calls `createEvent` once per destination calendar, passing the whole event with all hosts' destination calendars. Only Google uses the `credentialId` argument to pick its own destination. Office365 (here), Lark, and CalDAV (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`) always use the first entry (`mainHostDestinationCalendar`) regardless of whose credential is being used. For a collective event where a team member has Office365/CalDAV/Lark and the main host has a different calendar, the member's service is given the main host's externalId. For Office365 this POSTs to `/me/calendars/<wrong id>/events` and fails. For CalDAV the filter matches no calendar, nothing is created, and the call still reports success. The multi-host fix therefore only works for Google.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel deletion now repeats once per calendar reference
findings.body: The calendar-reference handling was changed from `find` to a `for...of` over all `_calendar` references. The recurring branch (`recurringEvent && recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings`) inside the loop deletes events for every user credential and every updated booking, independent of the current `reference`. With N calendar references (now common with multiple hosts), the full set of deletions runs N times. This causes duplicate delete calls and rate-limit or error noise for providers that don't treat a missing event as success. The recurring deletion should run once outside the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts organization slug / requestedSlug logic
findings.body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`. The `slug` column was set only when billing is disabled, and deferred via `requestedSlug` when billing is enabled. The new code is `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which inverts the first condition. With billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are now created without a slug. With billing enabled, the slug is set before payment while `requestedSlug` is also set. This has nothing to do with destination calendars and should be reverted or split into its own PR.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op. Collective team members who do have destination calendars get no calendar events, and EventManager falls back to the generic path. Initialise the array (e.g. `[]`) and push to it, rather than relying on a possibly-null value. Duplicates are also possible if a member's destination equals the organizer's.

findings.title: Unrelated rewrite of loadUsers changes selection and error behaviour
findings.body: `loadUsers` was rewritten as part of this PR. The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug } }`. An empty or undefined `dynamicUserList` now throws, and the catch turns it into an HttpError 500 "Unable to load users". Neither change is described by the PR or needed for the destination-calendar work, and the dropped organization field may be needed by downstream code. This should be reverted or justified and tested separately.

findings.title: Webhook/API payload shape for destinationCalendar changes from object to array
findings.body: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is serialized into webhook payloads (see the updated e2e expectation `destinationCalendar: []`). Changing it from a single object to an array is a breaking contract change for webhook subscribers and API consumers. The PR is labelled non-breaking and has no migration note. It is also inconsistent: BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED can still emit `null` (handleNewBooking) while other flows emit `[]`.

findings.title: No tests for new multi-destination calendar logic
findings.body: The PR changes the core `CalendarEvent` contract and adds multi-credential create/update/delete flows across EventManager, CalendarManager, handleCancelBooking, and several calendar services. No unit or e2e tests cover multiple destination calendars, the credential DB-lookup fallback, or the empty/null cases. The checklist states no tests were added. The regressions above (Meet fallback crash, video credentialId, Google fallback lookup) would have been caught by basic tests.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId for calendar updates
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` results contain neither field, so calendar references created by `updateLocation` (and any update results) have both undefined. Previously they were filled from the event's destinationCalendar. Those references then take the legacy 'run through every credential' path on cancellation instead of using the exact credential and calendar.
